title: Propositional logic
primary_statement: connectives and truth-functional reasoning

title: Predicate logic
primary_statement: quantifiers over a domain, bound variables

title: Negation of quantifiers
primary_statement: not forall x P(x) iff exists x not P(x) ; not exists iff forall not

title: Quantifier order
primary_statement: forall x exists y is weaker than exists y forall x

title: Proof by contradiction, contrapositive, cases
primary_statement: classical proof strategies

title: Axiom of extensionality
primary_statement: sets with the same elements are equal

title: Axiom of the empty set
primary_statement: there is a set with no elements

title: Axiom of pairing
primary_statement: for any a,b the set {a,b} exists

title: Axiom of union
primary_statement: for any set F the union of its members exists

title: Axiom of power set
primary_statement: for any set X the set of all subsets of X exists

title: Axiom schema of separation
primary_statement: { x in X : phi(x) } is a set for any formula phi

title: Axiom schema of replacement
primary_statement: the image of a set under a definable class function is a set

title: Axiom of infinity
primary_statement: there is an inductive set

title: Axiom of foundation
primary_statement: membership is well-founded; no infinite descending epsilon-chains

title: Axiom of choice
primary_statement: every family of nonempty sets has a choice function

title: Axiom of countable choice
primary_statement: a countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function

title: Axiom of dependent choice
primary_statement: a total relation admits an infinite chain

title: Zermelo-Fraenkel set theory
primary_statement: the nine ZF axioms

title: ZFC
primary_statement: ZF plus the axiom of choice

title: Set
primary_statement: an element of a model of ZFC

title: Empty set
primary_statement: the unique set with no elements

title: Subset
primary_statement: A subset B iff every element of A is in B

title: Power set
primary_statement: P(X) is the set of all subsets of X

title: Union and intersection
primary_statement: A cup B, A cap B

title: Union and intersection of a family
primary_statement: union F ; intersection F (F nonempty)

title: Indexed family
primary_statement: a function i -> A_i on an index set I

title: Indexed union and intersection
primary_statement: union over i of A_i ; intersection over i (I nonempty)

title: Set difference
primary_statement: A minus B = { x in A : x not in B }

title: Relative complement
primary_statement: X^c = U minus X relative to an ambient U

title: De Morgan's laws
primary_statement: complement of a union is the intersection of complements, and dually

title: Distributive laws for sets
primary_statement: A cap union B_i = union (A cap B_i)

title: Ordered pair
primary_statement: (a,b) = {{a},{a,b}} ; (a,b)=(c,d) iff a=c and b=d

title: Cartesian product
primary_statement: X x Y = { (x,y) : x in X, y in Y }

title: Disjoint union
primary_statement: X + Y = (X x {0}) cup (Y x {1})

title: Binary relation
primary_statement: a subset of X x Y

title: Domain and range
primary_statement: dom R and ran R

title: Composition and inverse of relations
primary_statement: S o R and R^{-1}

title: Properties of relations
primary_statement: reflexive, symmetric, antisymmetric, transitive, connex

title: Restriction of a relation
primary_statement: R restricted to A

title: Equivalence relation
primary_statement: reflexive, symmetric, transitive

title: Partition
primary_statement: nonempty pairwise-disjoint sets covering X

title: Equivalence relations correspond to partitions
primary_statement: equivalence relations on X are in bijection with partitions of X

title: Quotient set
primary_statement: X/~ is the set of equivalence classes

title: Well-definedness on a quotient
primary_statement: [x] -> f(x) is a function iff x~x' implies f(x)=f(x')

title: Universal property of the quotient
primary_statement: functions X/~ -> Z are exactly functions X -> Z constant on classes

title: Function
primary_statement: a single-valued relation, total on its domain, with a fixed codomain

title: Injection
primary_statement: f(x)=f(y) implies x=y

title: Surjection
primary_statement: every y in the codomain has a preimage

title: Bijection
primary_statement: injective and surjective

title: Image of a set
primary_statement: f[A] = { f(x) : x in A }

title: Preimage of a set
primary_statement: f^{-1}[B] = { x : f(x) in B } , defined for every f

title: Preimage algebra
primary_statement: f^{-1} commutes with arbitrary union, arbitrary intersection, and complement

title: Image algebra
primary_statement: f[union A_i] = union f[A_i] ; f[intersection A_i] subset intersection f[A_i]

title: Composition of functions
primary_statement: (g o f)(x) = g(f(x))

title: Identity function
primary_statement: id_X(x) = x

title: Inverse function
primary_statement: g with g o f = id and f o g = id

title: Invertible iff bijective
primary_statement: f has a two-sided inverse iff f is a bijection

title: Left inverse iff injective
primary_statement: f has a left inverse iff f is injective (domain nonempty)

title: Right inverse iff surjective
primary_statement: f has a right inverse iff f is surjective (uses choice)

title: Composition preserves inj/surj/bij
primary_statement: composites of injections are injections, etc.

title: Function space
primary_statement: Y^X is the set of all functions X -> Y

title: P(X) is isomorphic to 2^X
primary_statement: A -> 1_A is a bijection P(X) -> 2^X

title: Pigeonhole principle
primary_statement: no injection from a finite set into a strictly smaller one

title: Partial order
primary_statement: reflexive, antisymmetric, transitive

title: Total order
primary_statement: a partial order in which any two elements are comparable

title: Strict order
primary_statement: irreflexive and transitive

title: Order-preserving map and order isomorphism
primary_statement: x <= y implies f(x) <= f(y) ; bijective order embedding

title: Bounds, suprema, maxima
primary_statement: upper/lower bound, sup/inf, max/min

title: Chain and antichain
primary_statement: a totally ordered / pairwise-incomparable subset

title: Maximal and minimal element
primary_statement: m with no element strictly above it

title: Well-order
primary_statement: a total order in which every nonempty subset has a least element

title: Zorn's lemma
primary_statement: a poset in which every chain has an upper bound has a maximal element

title: Well-ordering theorem
primary_statement: every set can be well-ordered

title: Equivalents of the axiom of choice
primary_statement: AC iff Zorn iff well-ordering iff cardinal comparability

title: Ordinal
primary_statement: a transitive set well-ordered by membership

title: Transfinite induction
primary_statement: if a property passes to alpha whenever it holds below alpha it holds for all ordinals

title: Transfinite recursion
primary_statement: a class function on ordinals is uniquely determined by a rule using its earlier values

title: Order type
primary_statement: every well-order is isomorphic to a unique ordinal

title: Construction of the natural numbers
primary_statement: omega is the smallest inductive set ; 0 = empty set, S x = x cup {x}

title: Finite ordinal / natural number
primary_statement: an element of omega

title: The Peano axioms hold in omega
primary_statement: (omega, 0, S) satisfies the Peano axioms

title: Recursion theorem on omega
primary_statement: unique f on omega with f(0)=a and f(S n)=g(n, f n)

title: Equinumerosity
primary_statement: |X| = |Y| iff there is a bijection X -> Y

title: Cardinal comparison
primary_statement: |X| <= |Y| iff there is an injection X -> Y

title: Strict cardinal comparison
primary_statement: |X| < |Y| iff |X| <= |Y| and not |X| = |Y|

title: Cantor-Schroeder-Bernstein
primary_statement: injections both ways give a bijection ; no choice needed

title: Cantor's theorem
primary_statement: |X| < |P(X)| for every set X

title: Finite set
primary_statement: equinumerous with some finite ordinal

title: Infinite set
primary_statement: not finite

title: Dedekind-infinite set
primary_statement: equinumerous with a proper subset of itself

title: Finite iff not Dedekind-infinite
primary_statement: over ZF + countable choice, the two notions of infinite coincide

title: Countable set
primary_statement: admits an injection into omega

title: omega x omega is countable
primary_statement: the Cantor pairing is a bijection omega x omega -> omega

title: Countable sets are closed under the usual operations
primary_statement: subsets, images, finite products, and countable unions of countable sets are countable

title: Uncountable set
primary_statement: infinite and not countable

title: The diagonal argument
primary_statement: 2^omega is uncountable

title: P(omega) has the cardinality of the continuum
primary_statement: |P(omega)| = |2^omega| = |R|

title: Comparability of cardinals
primary_statement: for any X,Y either |X| <= |Y| or |Y| <= |X| (uses AC)

title: Arithmetic of infinite cardinals
primary_statement: aleph0 + aleph0 = aleph0*aleph0 = aleph0 ; kappa*kappa = kappa for infinite kappa (AC)

title: Hartogs' number
primary_statement: for every X there is a well-ordered cardinal that does not inject into X ; no choice

title: The aleph hierarchy
primary_statement: aleph_alpha enumerates the infinite well-ordered cardinals

title: The continuum
primary_statement: c = 2^aleph0 = |R|

title: The continuum hypothesis
primary_statement: no cardinal strictly between aleph0 and 2^aleph0 ; independent of ZFC
